name: Screamer
description: A wiry punk karaoke singer in his thirties who always chooses the loudest song; jagged and theatrical without reading as violent.
build: Wiry, angular, lean and spring-tensioned with thin bare arms and heavy grounded boots; never broad, soft or bulky.
hair: Six or seven separate asymmetric rigid amber hair spikes drawn as distinct angular wedges. Never a mohawk or a soft hair mass.
outfit: A black sleeveless patched denim vest over a bare chest, a simple studded belt, black jeans with two small horizontal knee tears, and heavy black boots with amber laces. Patches are abstract pixel shapes without readable text.
performance_style: Leans back from the waist with the lead boot forward, the rear boot set wide, knees flexed, the character-right hand clenched at chest height, and the free arm flung open with an open hand.
location: A basement punk venue: a cracked grey concrete floor running to the bottom of the frame, a low ceiling of exposed ducts and pipes crowded with layered flyers and stickers, a back wall of chipped black paint under a hundred more, a battered half-stack and a coil of cable shoved into one corner, and two bare clamp lights throwing harsh white glare and hard shadows.
recognition_cues: six or seven separate asymmetric rigid amber hair spikes drawn as distinct angular wedges
avoid: clothing spikes beyond small belt studs
readable tattoos, patches, or band names

dance.intent: Punk karaoke dance loop: rock between the lead boot and wide rear boot, let the amber hair spikes and vest edge follow, punch the open free hand upward once, then return to the spring-tensioned opening without attacking.

sing.intent: Loud vocal loop: lean back through the flexed knees, throw the free arm open, then recover into the heavy planted stance. The mouth must visibly open and change shape across the loop so he unmistakably reads as singing.

animations.flinch: Brief room-sound surprise: amber spikes and open free hand snap outward, the torso recoils slightly, then he regains his wiry planted performance pose. No opponent, strike, or contact.
animations.guard: One-shot stage self-protection: tighten the vest-side torso line, bring the open free hand across the body, then hold a grounded final stance. Not combat.
animations.entrance: One-shot entrance: stride in with heavy boots and wiry tension, flare the open free hand and hair spikes toward the room, then land in the canonical leaned-back performance stance.
animations.victory: One-shot performance finish: raise the open free hand in a theatrical acknowledgement, let the spikes and vest settle, then hold a loud proud balanced final pose.
animations.ko: Non-contact performance defeat: he stays on his feet while the spring tension drops out of the wiry frame all at once — the thin bare arms go slack, the free hand opens and falls, and his head hangs low with the chin toward his chest. The amber hair spikes stay separate and angular as they tip forward He holds a standing, visibly defeated finish and remains standing on both planted feet in every frame — no kneeling, crouching, sitting, sinking, or going to the ground. Do not imply injury, impact, or an opponent.
